hypotheses.reasoning: At 01:34:07 redis-cache was replaced and came back with 0 keys (#173). The cache miss ratio then jumped to 92% (#177), so nearly every read went straight to catalog-db. The database hit CPU 100% with connections near the 500 limit (#180), and simple product-by-id lookups took 3-8s (#185). search-api's product queries then hit their 5s timeout (#192, #212), and web-bff returned 504s. This is a cache stampede: the empty cache alone would have been survivable, but every miss hitting the database is what caused the outage.

A second reading of the same lines: catalog-db got slow and the calls to it timed out. But nothing shows a lock or a separate fault in the database, so the slowness looks like load from the empty cache.

verdict.recommendedAction: Warm the redis cache back up (preload hot product keys). Add request coalescing or a single-flight guard so cache misses don't all hit catalog-db at once, and rate-limit how fast misses can load from the database. Turn on RDB/AOF persistence so a replaced node doesn't start empty.
